pages.title: Nigeria Digital Payment Fraud 2025: Losses Down 51%
pages.text:
# Nigeria Digital Payment Fraud 2025: Losses Down 51%

For years, the narrative surrounding Nigerian fintech has been dominated by a singular, persistent anxiety: the soaring cost of digital fraud. Headlines have consistently warned of staggering losses, painting a picture of an ecosystem where every transaction carries an inherent risk. But the data from the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) tells a different story for 2025. According to recent reports, digital payment fraud losses have plummeted by 51%, dropping from ₦52.26bn in 2024 to ₦25.85bn in 2025. This shift is not just a statistical anomaly; it represents a fundamental change in how Nigeria manages financial risk.

## Understanding the Nigeria Digital Payment Fraud 2025 Shift

This decline in **Nigeria digital payment fraud 2025** is not a fluke. It is the result of a coordinated effort between the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), NIBSS, and commercial banks to tighten the screws on illicit activity. The core of this change lies in the friction created by security protocols. While users often complain about the inconvenience of multi-factor authentication or biometric verification, this ‘friction’ is exactly what stalled the attackers.

By integrating BVN (Bank Verification Number) and NIN (National Identity Number) mandates more strictly, financial institutions have made it significantly harder for bad actors to operate anonymous ‘mule’ accounts. When the cost of acquiring a verified identity becomes higher than the potential payout of a fraudulent transaction, the economics of cybercrime fall apart.

| Metric | 2024 | 2025 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total Fraud Loss | ₦52.26bn | ₦25.85bn |
| Trend | High Baseline | 51% Reduction |

## The Privacy vs. Security Trade-off

As a privacy advocate, it is essential to acknowledge the trade-off. We are trading a degree of anonymity for a substantial increase in systemic security. For Gen Z Nigerians and digital natives who are used to instant transactions, this shift manifests as more frequent re-authentication requests and stricter transaction limits on unverified accounts. This is a clear exercise of [data protection](https://privacyneedle.com/data-protection/) principles—using personal data (biometrics) to ensure the integrity of the financial system. However, the centralization of this data creates its own set of risks, which [compliance](https://privacyneedle.com/compliance/) teams across the continent are closely watching.

## Separating Facts from Speculation

While the reduction in fraud losses is verified, it is important to distinguish between successful prevention and sophisticated displacement. Experts suggest that as banks harden their defenses, attackers shift their focus toward social engineering—tricking the user rather than hacking the bank. You are no longer just fighting a technical threat; you are fighting the psychological manipulation of users. This is a critical distinction for [tech security](https://privacyneedle.com/tech-security/) teams who must now focus on human-centric defense mechanisms alongside their firewall investments.

## Real-Life Scenario: The Pivot

Consider a typical small business owner in Lagos. In 2024, they might have dealt with frequent chargeback frauds from compromised accounts. In 2025, those same attackers, finding it harder to open new accounts, have pivoted to phishing campaigns aimed at obtaining the owner’s banking login details. The *method* of the theft has changed, even if the *target* remains the same. This illustrates why users cannot become complacent just because the aggregate national fraud numbers are down.

## Practical Steps to Stay Secure

The numbers show we are moving in the right direction, but individual vigilance remains the primary line of defense. Here is what you should do immediately to protect your assets:

- **Enable App-Level Biometrics:** Do not rely on a simple PIN. Ensure your banking app requires a fingerprint or FaceID for every transaction, not just login.
- **Monitor Transaction Alerts:** Set your push notifications to alert you for any transaction, regardless of size. Immediate awareness is the best way to stop unauthorized movement.
- **Audit Linked Accounts:** Regularly check your settings to see which third-party apps have access to your bank information via APIs. Revoke access for any service you no longer use.
- **Verify Requests via Direct Channels:** If you receive a call from ‘customer service’ asking for your OTP or BVN, hang up. Call your bank using the official number on the back of your debit card or their verified website, [NIBSS](https://nibss-plc.com.ng/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why did fraud losses fall so sharply in 2025?

The reduction is largely attributed to stricter enforcement of BVN and NIN linking, improved AI-driven fraud detection systems in banks, and enhanced real-time inter-bank monitoring.

### Does this mean my data is safer?

Your assets are technically more secure from unauthorized access, but your personal data is being processed more extensively. Always ensure you are interacting only with regulated, licensed financial institutions.

## Conclusion

The 51% reduction in Nigeria digital payment fraud 2025 is a landmark win for the nation’s financial stability. It proves that when policy, technology, and identity verification align, the ecosystem becomes hostile to cybercriminals. However, as the digital gatekeepers get stronger, attackers will evolve. By remaining aware of the risks and maintaining strict control over your personal data, you contribute to a safer, more robust financial future for everyone in the ecosystem.

Three winners have been selected in the 2025 edition of the WIPO National Intellectual Property Essay Competition, an initiative that highlights the power of intellectual property (IP) to drive economic and creative growth.

This year’s edition, launched on April 30, 2025, invited students to reflect on “*IP and Music: Harnessing Nigeria’s Music Industry for Economic Growth”, aligning with the broader 2025 World IP Day theme*“, IP and music: Feel the beat of IP”.

Participating students were challenged to critically reflect on how the creativity of artists, producers, and other stakeholders in Nigeria’s music industry, supported by strong IP frameworks, can contribute significantly to the nation’s economy. An independent panel of 20 judges reviewed 188 essays from 57 tertiary institutions across 26 states, selecting the top three winners alongside 17 finalists.

pages.title: How seven payment gateways stack up for Nigerian businesses – Businessday NG
pages.text:
# How seven payment gateways stack up for Nigerian businesses – Businessday NG

Nigeria’s booming electronic payments market is forcing businesses to think beyond simply accepting money online as the choice of payment gateway increasingly affects transaction costs, settlement speed, reliability and the ability to reach customers at home and abroad.

The scale of the market shows why that choice matters. Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System Plc (NIBSS) processed more than 11.2 billion instant-payment transactions valued at over N1.07 quadrillion in 2024, while the Central Bank of Nigeria recorded about N3.46 quadrillion in electronic payments across nearly 48 billion transactions in 2025.

Read also: [MTN’s 100m subscribers open data, fintech opportunity](https://businessday.ng/technology/article/mtns-100m-subscribers-open-data-fintech-opportunity/)

With the CBN’s Payments System Vision 2028 also positioning Nigeria as a regional payments hub, competition among payment infrastructure providers is increasingly shifting from basic payment acceptance to scale, speed, connectivity, security and cross-border capability.

For businesses, that means the gateway with the lowest headline fee is not necessarily the cheapest or most suitable option. Settlement time, payment success rates, available channels, integration requirements and access to broader financial infrastructure can have a bigger effect on the cost of doing business.

Seven major providers illustrate the different strategies now competing for Nigerian merchants: Paystack, Monnify, Flutterwave, Interswitch, Squad, Nomba and Paga.

**Paystack combines simplicity with scale**

Paystack remains one of the strongest options for businesses seeking a relatively straightforward route into online payments.

The company charges 1.5 percent plus N100 for local transactions, capped at N2,000, while the N100 component is waived for transactions below N2,500. International transactions attract a 3.9 percent fee plus N100.

Settlement is generally the next business day. Founded in 2015 and acquired by Stripe in 2020, Paystack has built its position partly around ease of onboarding and developer-friendly integration. It has more than 200,000 merchants and supports cards, bank transfers, USSD, QR codes, Apple Pay, mobile money and payment links.

Its scale also provides an indication of market penetration. Paystack processed N1 trillion in a single month in July 2024, becoming the first Nigerian gateway to reach that level.

For businesses, its attraction is less about having the cheapest price and more about combining a mature developer experience, multiple payment channels, fraud controls and access to Stripe’s global technology ecosystem.

**Monnify leans on banking infrastructure**

Monnify competes differently, using its connection to TeamApt and the wider Moniepoint ecosystem to emphasise payment infrastructure and settlement.

It charges 1.5 percent on local transactions, capped at N2,000, and four percent on international transactions. Its headline differentiator is settlement, which is offered instantly.

Monnify processed about N25 trillion in transaction value in 2025, equivalent to roughly $18 billion, representing a 38 percent increase from 2023. It has more than 100,000 merchants across 27 Nigerian banks.

The platform offers virtual accounts, payment links, cards, bank transfers, USSD, direct debit, offline payments and disbursements.

That makes it particularly relevant to businesses that need more than a checkout page. Companies collecting money at scale can use virtual accounts and other payment infrastructure to manage flows across different customer and business segments.

**Flutterwave offers the broadest cross-border proposition**

Flutterwave’s biggest advantage is geographic reach. The company operates across more than 30 countries and supports payments in more than 30 currencies, giving Nigerian businesses selling into other African markets or international markets an infrastructure advantage.

Its customer base includes major global companies such as Uber, Microsoft, MTN and Wise. The trade-off is cost. Local transactions attract a two percent fee, capped at N2,000, following an increase from 1.4 percent in April 2025. International transactions cost 4.8 percent.

For a purely domestic business processing large volumes, that pricing can make cheaper gateways more attractive. For an exporter, digital business or company collecting from customers across multiple markets, however, the additional cost can be justified by the broader payment network.

Flutterwave supports cards, bank transfers, USSD, mobile money, NQR, eNaira and other payment methods.

**Interswitch offers institutional depth**

Interswitch is the oldest provider in the group, having been founded in 2002, and its competitive advantage is the depth of its financial infrastructure rather than startup-style simplicity.

Its WebPAY product charges 1.5 percent for local transactions, capped at N2,000, with a N150,000 one-time setup fee. International transactions attract 3.5 percent, while settlement is generally the next day.

The company processed 1.2 billion transactions in March 2023 alone, demonstrating the scale of the infrastructure behind its business.

Its ecosystem includes the Verve card scheme, Quickteller and a network of more than 11,000 ATMs.

For large organisations that prioritise institutional relationships, proven infrastructure and deep integration with the Nigerian financial system, that history can be more important than the absence of a setup fee.

For smaller businesses, however, the N150,000 setup cost can make other gateways easier to adopt.

**Squad brings banking relationships into the gateway market**

Squad, the payments business of HabariPay and part of GTCO, brings another banking-led model to the market.

The company processed N27.4 trillion in transaction value in 2024, putting it among the higher-volume payment platforms operating in Nigeria.

Unlike several competitors, Squad does not publicly list a standard transaction fee in the information available for comparison, making direct price comparisons more difficult.

Its proposition is built around access to GTCO’s banking ecosystem, while its payment tools include cards, bank transfers, USSD, virtual accounts, payment links and soft POS.

That combination gives businesses the ability to connect online and offline collections through a single platform. Its appeal is therefore likely to be strongest for businesses that value banking relationships and integrated payment infrastructure alongside the gateway itself.

**Nomba competes aggressively on price**

Nomba has one of the clearest cost propositions among the seven. Its local transaction fee is 1.4 percent, capped at N1,800, while international transactions cost 3.9 percent. Businesses processing at least N50 million monthly can also negotiate volume discounts.

The company has more than 600,000 merchants and processes more than N3 trillion in monthly transaction value.

That scale reflects Nomba’s roots in physical merchant payments. The company, formerly known as Kudi, has expanded from agent and point-of-sale services into a broader payments platform combining physical and digital commerce.

Its recent expansion includes Apple Pay on physical POS terminals and a partnership with UK open-banking platform Volume to enable Nigerian merchants to collect pounds directly from UK bank accounts.

For high-volume domestic merchants, its lower fee and N1,800 cap can be significant. A business processing millions of naira every month can see small differences in transaction charges accumulate into substantial costs.

**Paga’s advantage is reach beyond digital-first customers**

Paga occupies a different part of the market. Founded in 2009 and licensed by the CBN as a mobile money operator, the company combines digital payments with a large agent network.

Its account-funding service is free, while local card transactions attract a 1.5 percent fee. International transactions cost 3.5 percent, with settlement ranging from real time to the next day.

Paga supports mobile money, bank transfers, cards, USSD and wallet payments. Its physical distribution network gives it an advantage among businesses whose customers are not entirely digital-first, particularly those serving rural markets, informal businesses and customers who rely heavily on mobile money.

For such businesses, reach can matter more than having the lowest online transaction fee.

**The choice is increasingly about fit**

The comparison shows that Nigeria’s payment gateway market is no longer a simple contest over transaction charges.

Read also:[CBN tells banks, fintechs to treat cyber risk as financial stability threat](https://businessday.ng/uncategorized/article/cbn-tells-banks-fintechs-to-treat-cyber-risk-as-financial-stability-threat/)

Paystack’s strength is its combination of ease of use, technology and scale. Monnify competes on banking infrastructure and settlement. Flutterwave is strongest where cross-border payments matter. Interswitch brings institutional depth, while Squad leverages banking relationships. Nomba combines aggressive pricing with physical and digital payments, and Paga differentiates itself through its agent and mobile-money reach.

For a small online business, a gateway with simple integration and no setup fee may be the logical starting point. A large merchant may care more about volume pricing, transaction reliability and settlement. A company selling across Africa may accept higher fees in exchange for multi-currency infrastructure, while a business serving less-bankable customers may value agent and wallet networks.

The broader lesson is that payment infrastructure is becoming a strategic business decision rather than a back-office utility.

As Nigeria’s electronic payments market expands, businesses that compare gateways on the full cost and capability of moving money, not just the percentage displayed on a pricing page, will be better positioned to reduce payment friction, improve cash flow and scale.

***Data sources: CBN, NIBSS, individual payment gateway pricing pages and company disclosures. Fees and product terms may change, and businesses should verify current charges and settlement conditions directly with providers before making a decision.***

- Stablecoins: ❌
- Traditional Cards: ✅ Visa, Mastercard
- Digital Wallets: ✅ Apple Pay, Google Pay
- Bank Transfer: ✅ ACH, SEPA

**Transaction Fees.** Local transaction fees for Interswitch typically hover around 1.5%, with additional fees for international transactions. The fee structure includes a cap (often around ₦2,000) which stabilizes costs on larger payments and makes budgeting easier for merchants. Although its pricing can be higher than some competitors, Interswitch’s reliability and institutional backing justify the cost for many businesses. Fee negotiations may be possible for enterprise accounts.

| Fee Type | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Local Transactions | ~1.5% |
| International | ~2% |

**Transaction Speed.** Interswitch transactions usually settle within 24 hours, which helps merchants streamline cash flow and reduces payment delays. Its mature processing network facilitates efficient clearing and settlement across banks. A consistent transaction speed enhances trust among buyers and sellers. Interswitch’s robust system also supports high volumes without significant slowdowns.

- Payment Processing: 24 hours
- Funds Availability: 24 hours
- Payout to Bank: 1-2 Business Days
- 24/7 Operation: ✅
![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%201%201'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## Remita

[Remita](https://www.remita.net/) is a Nigerian payment services platform that has been widely used across both private businesses and government institutions for payments and collections since its establishment in 2003. It is particularly known for facilitating large volumes of transactions, including salaries, fees, and utility payments. Remita’s payment gateway integrates with numerous channels like cards, bank transfers, and USSD. Its strength lies in comprehensive financial management tools and institutional credibility that supports enterprises and public sectors.

**Supported Payment Methods.** Remita offers support for cards, bank transfers, USSD, POS, and other payment channels, allowing merchants to accept payments from a variety of customer preferences. This multi‑channel support enables seamless transactions for both online and offline commerce. The platform also integrates financial reporting and reconciliation tools. Remita’s flexibility makes it suitable for complex payment environments like schools, NGOs, and large enterprises.

- Number of Currencies: 50+
- Stablecoins: ❌
- Traditional Cards: ✅ Visa, Mastercard
- Digital Wallets: ✅ Apple Pay, Google Pay
- Bank Transfer: ✅ ACH, SEPA

**Transaction Fees.** Remita’s transaction fees are typically around 2% for local payments (reviewed with caps and variations depending on volume) and may be higher for international cards, reflecting its focus on enterprise‑level services. The fee may vary for large institutional accounts and often depends on negotiated terms. Transparent pricing helps businesses plan costs accordingly. Higher fees may be justified by advanced features such as reconciliation reporting.

| Fee Type | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Local Transactions | ~2% |
| International | ~2% |

**Transaction Speed.** Remita usually processes and settles transactions within 24 hours, especially for standard online payments. Its system design also supports same‑day or next‑day payouts in many cases. This speed benefits businesses managing payroll, fees, and institutional payments that require reliable settlement timing. Fast processing enhances operational efficiency for larger organizations.

- Payment Processing: 24 hours
- Funds Availability: 24 hours
- Payout to Bank: 1 Business Day
- 24/7 Operation: ✅
![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%201%201'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## Conclusion

In this review, we have analyzed the top payment gateways for businesses in Nigeria, including NOWPayments, Paystack, Flutterwave, Interswitch, and Remita. Each gateway has unique features tailored to specific business needs, but when it comes to the Nigerian market’s evolving demand for cryptocurrency adoption, global payments, and fast transactions, NOWPayments emerges as the clear leader. Its support for over 350 cryptocurrencies, alongside traditional payment methods like Visa, Mastercard, and PayPal, ensures that Nigerian businesses can reach both local and international customers seamlessly.

[NOWPayments](https://nowpayments.io/) stands out not only for its impressive range of supported payment methods but also for its highly competitive fee structure, offering 0.5% for transactions without conversion and 1% for those with conversion, along with zero network fees for USDT TRC20 deposits for the first two months. Its fast processing speeds and instant settlements make it an ideal choice for businesses seeking reliability and efficiency. As the optimal solution for forward-thinking businesses in Nigeria, NOWPayments provides the flexibility, cost-efficiency, and security needed to thrive in a rapidly changing digital payments landscape.

| Moniepoint Inc. | |

**Moniepoint** (formerly **TeamApt**) is a Nigerian [fintech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fintech "Fintech") company based in [Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos "Lagos") that provides [banking services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banking_services "Banking services") and [loans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan "Loan") via an [online banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_banking "Online banking") app. The company was founded by [Tosin Eniolorunda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tosin_Eniolorunda "Tosin Eniolorunda") and Felix Ike in 2015. In November 2024, Bayo Olujobi was appointed its [chief financial officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_financial_officer "Chief financial officer") (CFO).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-2)

## History

Moniepoint was founded in 2015 by business executives [Tosin Eniolorunda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tosin_Eniolorunda "Tosin Eniolorunda") and Felix Ike.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-3) It was initially founded under the name, TeamApt.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-Tech_cabal-4)

In March 2019, Moniepoint announced funding of $5.5 million in a Series A fundraising from Quantum Capital Partners.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-5) In November 2019, Moniepoint received a switching license from the [Central Bank of Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Nigeria "Central Bank of Nigeria").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-7)

In 2021, the company announced an undisclosed capital in a Series B Funding round led by Novastar Ventures. It also fundraised the $50 million in pre-series C funding led by QED investors.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-8)

In March 2023, Moniepoint led the $3 million seed investment round for Nigerian [neobank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neobank "Neobank") Payday.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-9)

In July 2023, the company launched its personal banking service.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-11) By January 2026, the [Central Bank of Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Nigeria "Central Bank of Nigeria") officially upgraded the operating license of its subsidiary, Moniepoint Microfinance Bank, to a national status.

In 2023, Moniepoint got listed by the [Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Times "Financial Times") as the *Second-Fastest Growing Company in Africa*.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-12)

In October 2024, Moniepoint became the African continent's eighth [unicorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicorn_(finance) "Unicorn (finance)") at a valuation of over US$1 billion after it announced a US$110 million Series C funding round. Development Partners International’s African Development Partners (ADP) III fund, Google’s Africa Investment Fund led the round. [[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-Google_among-13) Lightrock also participated in the round.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-Google_among-13)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-15)

In 2025, the company announced an extension of its Series C round, raising an additional $90 million and bringing the total Series C funding to over $200 million.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-18)

In 2025, Moniepoint Inc. reported the digital payment infrastructure is accelerating the growth of Nigeria's food service industry, projected to reach US$11.09 biilion in 2025. The report highlights innovation such as instant settlement, automated payment verification, and transaction-based lending as key drivers of efficiency, financial inclusion, and business growth.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-23)

In 2026, Moniepoint in partner with [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google"), Women Techmakers Lagos, hosted the "Break the Pattern" workshop to equip young Nigerian women with practical tech and AI skills. The programme combined hands-on training, a Buildathone, and leadership sessions, while reinforcing Moniepoint commitment to developing tech talent through initiatives sush as Women in Tech, DreamDevs, HatchDev, and the 3MTT programme.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-27)

In 2026, Moniepoint Inc. graduated the second cohort of its DreamDev Bootcamp, a nine-week training programme aimed at addressing African's shortage of software engineering talent. The initiative equips participants with advanced software development skills, mentorship, and hands-on experience to prepare them for enterprise-level engineering roles.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moniepoint_Inc.#cite_note-29)

# Moniepoint Celebrates A Decade Of Impact, Microfinance Bank Disburses Over ₦1 Trillion In Credit To Empower Small Businesses In 2025

Moniepoint Inc., Nigeria's definitive platform for small businesses and Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, today released its 2025 Year in Review, marking a decade of "financial happiness" and a transformative year of growth. Highlighting its role as the backbone of Nigeria's entrepreneurial economy with over 6 million active businesses, the company revealed that its microfinance bank has now disbursed over ₦1 trillion in credit to thousands of businesses from provision stores and supermarkets to building materials sellers.

![](https://eu-west-2.graphassets.com/AxQ8YTi9LTCrOeR0pPuwfz/cmkzh5d9eq5e607mlokwvs0i2)

It is worthy to note that on average these businesses experienced growth by more than 36% after accessing credit, signposting its primacy as a transformational growth level and instrument of deepening shared prosperity. Moniepoint uses alternative data points that include transaction histories, business patterns and payment behaviours in a bid to accommodate what traditional credit scoring misses to drive financial inclusion and access to credit. The company’s 2025 performance reinforces its role as a critical financial infrastructure which not only supports the Nigerian economy but also impacts everyday lives, creating immense value.

Founded in 2015 by Tosin Eniolorunda and Felix Ike, Moniepoint Inc (formerly known as TeamApt Inc) has established itself as the leading financial platform for Nigeria’s vast network of small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs), offering an integrated suite of services, including digital payments, business bank accounts, credit, foreign exchange (FX), and management tools.

During the year, as Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, now powering 8 out of every 10 in-person payments made across the country, Moniepoint MFB, the banking and payments subsidiary, processed ₦412 trillion in transaction value, handling more than 14 billion transactions. This clearly suggests that Moniepoint is well-positioned to play a greater role in Nigeria’s steady march towards a trillion-dollar economy by 2030.

"Our journey has been one of intentional evolution," said Tosin Eniolorunda, Group CEO and Founder of Moniepoint Inc. "What started as a passion to solve overlooked problems has evolved into a platform powering the dreams of millions. As 83% of employment in Africa exists in the informal economy, our mission to create financial happiness is an operational mandate that guides our product development, our market expansion, and our capital allocation decisions."

Beaming with enthusiasm, Eniolorunda continues, “Yet for all we have accomplished, we approach our second decade with the clarity that our work remains unfinished. As we enter this next chapter, we do so with strengthened conviction in our strategy, deepened partnerships with world-class institutional investors, and an organisation scaled to deliver on Africa's entrepreneurial potential. The infrastructure we have built over the past decade provides the foundation. The journey is far from over, but our resolve has never been stronger. To our partners, our customers, and our team: thank you for a decade of impact. We are just getting started.”

In 2025, Moniepoint Inc. reached a series of critical inflexion points, highlighted by the successful completion of its Series C funding round, which raised over $200 million in equity financing from leading institutional investors, including Development Partners International, Google’s Africa Investment Fund, Visa, the International Finance Corporation, and Verod Capital. The year also marked the launch of MonieWorld in the United Kingdom, extending Moniepoint’s platform to serve the African diaspora by strengthening key remittance corridors and laying the foundation for the delivery of comprehensive cross-border financial services.

Moniepoint MFB re-launched its savings product in a firm demonstration of the company's commitment to its oft-stated mantra of providing financial happiness. Data reveals that, in terms of savings behavioural patterns, the majority of users choose to save on a daily basis, with focus across business operations (24%), rent (16.5%), and education (10%) representing top savings priorities. The launch of Moniebook and the acquisition of a national Microfinance Bank license for Moniepoint MFB further expand the company's regulated capabilities and product depth.

TeamApt Ltd, the switching and processing subsidiary of Moniepoint Inc., also achieved major regulatory and operational milestones in 2025 that have solidified its position in the global payments landscape. After a rigorous certification process, the company successfully secured licenses from Mastercard and Visa to act as a processor and acquirer for these global card schemes. This strategic move allows TeamApt to support international card payments directly and offer these critical switching services to other businesses across the continent. Monnify, the web payment gateway, processed N25 trillion in the period under review, demonstrating remarkable resilience and industry confidence, firmly positioning it for more business-to-business transactions.

Moniepoint’s impact extended beyond banking into critical social interventions, even as the company partnered with the Federal Government to support the Rice Intervention Programme, reaching nearly 850,000 beneficiaries, and worked with the Kaduna State Government in grants disbursement to vulnerable citizens. Through these initiatives, Moniepoint continues to build the infrastructure required to unlock Africa’s entrepreneurial potential, positioning itself as a trusted partner for the delivery of large-scale economic empowerment programmes.

As Moniepoint Inc. enters its second decade, its well-chronicled decade-long evolution from a backend technology provider to a household name directly complements the Nigerian government's vision of a more inclusive, data-driven, and productive financial landscape. To read more about the 2025 Year in Review Report, visit [http://2025.moniepoint.com](http://2025.moniepoint.com/)

# Moniepoint Nigeria 2026: USSD Code, POS, Charges & Care

8 min read Updated Oct 8, 2026

Table of Contents

- [What *5573# does and what it costs](https://finnaija.ng/moniepoint#heading-36d30759)
- [There is no Moniepoint loan code](https://finnaija.ng/moniepoint#there-is-no-moniepoint-loan-code)
- [Transfer and POS charges in 2026](https://finnaija.ng/moniepoint#transfer-and-pos-charges-in-2026)
- [Is Moniepoint safe? Licence and deposit insurance](https://finnaija.ng/moniepoint#heading-af25fd47)
- [Scams: what Moniepoint never asks for](https://finnaija.ng/moniepoint#heading-9aeaaf94)

MONIEPOINT-NG-20261008The official Moniepoint USSD code is ***5573#**. It works on MTN, Airtel, Glo and 9mobile without data, and the same code serves both Personal and Business accounts. There is no separate business code and no USSD code for borrowing. If your phone is stolen or you spot a debit you did not make, dial ***5573*911#** from any phone to stop debits on your account. Since 22 August 2025 Moniepoint charges a flat ₦10 for each successful USSD transaction, on top of the ₦6.98 per session that mobile networks have deducted from airtime since 18 June 2025. Emergency blocking, OTP retrieval and account activation carry no Moniepoint fee.

## What *5573# does and what it costs

A USSD session now has two separate costs. The network charge of ₦6.98 per 120-second session comes out of your airtime, under the end-user billing model that telecom operators switched on on 18 June 2025 after the NCC's 2025 USSD pricing determination. Before that, banks deducted the same ₦6.98 from the account itself. The second cost is Moniepoint's own fee, which it introduced on 22 August 2025 to pay for keeping the channel reliable.

| What you want to do | Code | Moniepoint fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open the full menu | *5573# | ₦10 if a transaction is completed |
| Send money to a Moniepoint account | *5573*1*Amount*Account number# | ₦10 |
| Send money to another Nigerian bank | *5573*2*Amount*Account number# | ₦10 |
| Check balance and account details | *5573*5# | ₦10 |
| Buy airtime for yourself | *5573*Amount# | ₦10 |
| Buy data | *5573*4# | ₦10 |
| Stop debits, block or unblock account or card | *5573*911# | free |

The ₦6.98 network charge applies to every row, including the free ones. Codes such as *5577*911# and *3890# still circulate on blogs, but Moniepoint's own documentation uses *5573*911# for blocking and *5573*5# for the balance. USSD can be switched off for an account in the settings of the Personal or Business app, which is worth doing if you never use it.

## There is no Moniepoint loan code

Pages promising a «Moniepoint loan code» or a «code to borrow from Moniepoint» rank well, but the bank has no USSD shortcode for loans. Business credit, the working-capital loans and overdrafts, is offered only in the Moniepoint Business app and dashboard, based on two to three months of transaction history on the account. Repayment is taken automatically as a share of daily POS settlements and incoming deposits, so a loan reduces the cash a merchant receives each day until it is cleared. Moniepoint also lends to individuals through the Personal app under the Quickmonie name, for customers whose personal account is at least six months old. Rates, terms and the real cost of both products are on our page about the [Moniepoint loan interest rate](https://finnaija.ng/moniepoint-loan).

## Transfer and POS charges in 2026

Moniepoint charges a flat ₦20 for a transfer from a Business account or POS terminal to another bank. For cash withdrawals at a Moniepoint POS, the platform fee is 0.5% of the amount up to ₦20,000, so ₦50 on ₦10,000, and a flat ₦100 above ₦20,000. Terminals are leased rather than sold, and one that processes less than about ₦80,000 a day can be flagged as underperforming and reassigned.

Since 1 January 2026 the ₦50 levy on transfers of ₦10,000 or more is called stamp duty under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, and the sender now pays it. Until the end of 2025 it was deducted from the person receiving the money as the electronic money transfer levy. Transfers below ₦10,000, salary payments and transfers between your own accounts at the same bank are exempt. The rule applies to every bank and fintech, so it is the same at [OPay](https://finnaija.ng/opay) and PalmPay.

## Is Moniepoint safe? Licence and deposit insurance

Moniepoint MFB is a microfinance bank licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria. It received a digital microfinance licence in February 2022, and on 26 January 2026 the CBN announced that Moniepoint, OPay, Kuda, PalmPay and Paga had been moved to national microfinance bank status, which allows them to operate in all 36 states and the FCT and requires paid-up capital of ₦5 billion. Deposits are insured by the NDIC, but the cover for microfinance bank customers is ₦2 million per depositor, against ₦5 million at commercial banks. Keep balances above ₦2 million at a commercial bank if that protection matters to you. In 2024 the CBN fined Moniepoint and OPay ₦1 billion each over know-your-customer failures found in a routine review.

## Scams: what Moniepoint never asks for

Moniepoint says its staff will never start a private chat with you on WhatsApp or social media, never ask for screenshots of your login, and never request your PIN, OTP, password, BVN or NIN. In 2023 fact-checkers traced a Facebook page called «Moniepoint Overdraft» that promised instant loans and collected usernames and PINs through an outside form; the bank answered that it «will never request your OTP or business PIN at any point». Fake support accounts usually copy the logo and add underscores, dots or words like «help», «desk» or «agent» to the handle, and they reply to people who post complaints publicly. The genuine sites are moniepoint.com and support.moniepoint.com, and the genuine apps are Moniepoint Personal Banking and Moniepoint Business.

Since September 2024 the apps ask for a fingerprint, face scan or time-based code before transfers above ₦500,000 from a personal account and ₦5 million from a business account. If a transaction you do not recognise goes through, stop debits with *5573*911#, then report it through support.moniepoint.com. If the bank does not resolve it, you can complain to the CBN's Consumer Protection Department or to the FCCPC. Before taking credit from any lender, compare the cost with the [OPay loan](https://finnaija.ng/opay-loan) and other options regulated by the CBN.

## Share this article

## Moniepoint FAQ

The official code is *5573#, for both Personal and Business accounts, on MTN, Airtel, Glo and 9mobile without data. To stop debits after a theft or suspicious transaction, dial *5573*911# from any phone.

Since 22 August 2025 Moniepoint charges ₦10 for each successful USSD transaction such as a transfer, balance check, airtime or data purchase. The mobile network also deducts ₦6.98 per session from airtime. Emergency blocking, OTP retrieval and account activation have no Moniepoint fee.

No. Moniepoint has no USSD code for borrowing. Business working-capital loans and overdrafts are offered in the Moniepoint Business app, and personal loans (Quickmonie) in the Personal app for accounts at least six months old.

Since 1 January 2026 the ₦50 levy on transfers of ₦10,000 or more is stamp duty under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and is paid by the sender. Transfers below ₦10,000, salary payments and transfers between your own accounts at the same bank are exempt.

Yes, by the NDIC, up to ₦2 million per depositor, the limit for microfinance banks. Commercial bank deposits are covered up to ₦5 million.

## Related Articles

### [Moniepoint Loan Nigeria 2026: Business Rates and Terms](https://finnaija.ng/moniepoint-loan)

Moniepoint's working-capital loan is priced at an effective 24%–40% a year (about 1.8%–2.8% a month) plus a management fee, from ₦1,000,000 over 12–24 weeks. Personal (Quickmonie) loans now exist too, but only for Personal accounts at least six months old, and their rate is shown only in the app.

Jul 27, 2026

Lcredit offers a quick solution for financial needs in Nigeria. This guide breaks down how major banks like GTBank, Access Bank, Zenith Bank, First Bank, and UBA provide these revolving credit facilities, outlining eligibility, interest rates, and the application process. Understand the advantages and inherent risks before you apply.

Oct 29, 2026

This comprehensive guide clarifies what KMDC loans are, their purpose in India, and why they are not available through Nigerian banks like GTBank, Access Bank, Zenith Bank, First Bank, or UBA. We compare the features, eligibility, and application processes of these distinct financial products, highlighting the regulatory frameworks of the CBN and NDIC in Nigeria.

# Paystack

Nigerian financial technology company

| Paystack | |
| --- | --- |
| [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/Paystack_Logo.svg/250px-Paystack_Logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paystack_Logo.svg) | |
| Industry | Fintech |
| Founded | 2015 |
| Founder | [Shola Akinlade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shola_Akinlade "Shola Akinlade"), [Ezra Olubi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Olubi "Ezra Olubi") |
| Headquarters | Lagos, Nigeria |
| [Parent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parent_company "Parent company") | Stripe |
| Website | [Paystack.com](https://www.paystack.com) |

**Paystack** is a [Nigerian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerians "Nigerians") [financial technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_technology "Financial technology") company that provides payment processing services for businesses in Africa. Founded in 2015 by software engineers [Shola Akinlade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shola_Akinlade "Shola Akinlade") and [Ezra Olubi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Olubi "Ezra Olubi"), the company participated in the [Y Combinator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y_Combinator "Y Combinator") startup accelerator in 2016. In October 2020, Paystack was acquired by [Stripe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stripe,_Inc. "Stripe, Inc.") for over $200 million. At the time of the transaction, the company secured payments for approximately 60,000 merchants.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:2-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:0-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:1-3)

## History

Paystack was founded in 2015 by Nigerian computer science graduates [Shola Akinlade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shola_Akinlade "Shola Akinlade") and Ezra Olubi.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:2-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:1-3) The company later participated in the [Y Combinator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y_Combinator "Y Combinator") startup accelerator, receiving early-stage funding in Silicon Valley.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:2-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:4-4) Paystack publicly launched in 2016 after participating in Y Combinator's Winter 2016 cohort.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-5)

In October 2020, Stripe announced its acquisition of Paystack for over $200 million, marking one of the largest fintech acquisitions in Africa.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:0-2) As part of the deal, Stripe stated that Paystack would serve as a “growth engine for modern businesses in Africa,” with plans to support more businesses and consolidate the fragmented African payments market.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:5-6)

In November 2020, *[BBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_News "BBC News")* reported that Paystack processed over 50% of all web payments in Nigeria and served over 60,000 organizations, including [FedEx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedEx "FedEx"), UPS, and MTN. The article described Paystack as part of Africa’s expanding digital payments sector. BBC also reported that improved digital payment and clearing systems could help small businesses and traders across Africa save time and costs.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-7)

In May 2021, Paystack expanded its operations to South Africa, its first market expansion outside Nigeria following the Stripe acquisition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-8)

In November 2023, *[Bloomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News")* reported that Paystack was restructuring its operations, scaling back in Europe and the Middle East to focus on expanding within African markets.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-9)

## Funding

In 2016, Paystack raised $1.3 million in seed funding from investors, including [Tencent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent "Tencent") and [Comcast Ventures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comcast_Ventures "Comcast Ventures").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-10) In 2018, the company secured $8 million in a [Series A funding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Series_A_funding "Series A funding") round led by [Stripe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stripe,_Inc. "Stripe, Inc."), with participation from [Visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc."), and Tencent.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:5-6)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-11) In 2020, Stripe acquired Paystack for over $200 million, as part of its expansion into Africa. Prior to the acquisition, Paystack served around 60,000 businesses, processing both online and offline transactions.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:0-2)

## Global investment in African fintech

The acquisition of Paystack coincided with a period of increased foreign investment in African financial technology companies. Similar transactions during this period included [Network International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_International "Network International")'s acquisition of DPO Group for $288 million and WorldRemit's acquisition of [Sendwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendwave "Sendwave") for $500 million.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:3-12) Market analysts have attributed this investment trend to high mobile money adoption rates and a large unbanked population across the continent. Following the acquisition, multinational financial firms, including [Visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc."), [Mastercard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastercard "Mastercard"), [PayPal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PayPal "PayPal"), and [Tencent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent "Tencent"), also expanded their investments in African fintech startups.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:3-12) At the time of the transaction, [Stripe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stripe,_Inc. "Stripe, Inc.") co-founder Patrick Collison noted that online commerce in Africa was projected to grow by approximately 30% annually.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:5-6)

According to *[CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN")*, the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") contributed to increased [digital banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_banking "Digital banking") adoption across Africa, with Paystack reporting a fivefold rise in business sign-ups in 2020. Paystack co-founder Shola Akinlade stated that the pandemic highlighted how many African businesses lacked adequate digital infrastructure, making it challenging for them to transition to online transactions.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:2-1)

In April 2022, *[Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuters "Reuters")* reported that African startups raised $5.2 billion in venture capital in 2021, with fintech firms accounting for 60% of total investment. The article cited Paystack's acquisition by Stripe as an example of international interest in African startups.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:1-3)

In March 2025, [*Business Day*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BusinessDay_(Nigeria) "BusinessDay (Nigeria)") published an article stating that Africa’s e-commerce sector is expanding, driven by a growing middle class and increased [smartphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smartphone "Smartphone") adoption. It stated that, "as digital payments improve and trust in online shopping grows, e-commerce is expected to play a pivotal role in Africa’s economic transformation". The article also mentioned Paystack, along with [Flutterwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flutterwave "Flutterwave") and [M-Pesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-Pesa "M-Pesa"), as companies that have transformed the digital payments landscape and facilitated financial transactions across the continent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:4-4)

In 2026, Paystack announced the acquisition of Ladder Microfinance Bank, indicating a move beyond payment processing into other areas of financial services.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-14)

## Startup Act (2022)

Fintech is one of the fastest-growing tech sectors in Africa, providing [mobile money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_Money "Mobile Money"), digital payments, and lending solutions to unbanked populations. Nigeria has become a key hub for fintech startups, attracting investment and international expansion. In 2022, the Nigerian government enacted the Startup Act, which introduced tax incentives and funding mechanisms to support entrepreneurs.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-:4-4)

## Partnerships

- **2016:** Launched a payments solution integrated with [e-commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-commerce "E-commerce") platform [Shopify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shopify "Shopify") to allow more African retailers to sell their goods on the platform.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-15)
- **2021:** Selected as the preferred payment partner of [open-source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_source "Open source") e-commerce solution [WooCommerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WooCommerce "WooCommerce").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-16)
- **2021**: Introduced Pay with [Apple Pay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Pay "Apple Pay") on its platform.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-17)
- **2022:** Partnered with accounting software provider [Xero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xero_(company) "Xero (company)"), enabling Xero users in Africa to add a "Pay with Paystack" button to their invoices.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paystack#cite_note-18)

pages.title: What is Paystack and how does it work?
pages.text:
# What is Paystack and how does it work?

Paystack is a payment service provider that facilitates easy, fast and secure online and in-person payments for African businesses.

With our variety of no-code, low-code and pro-code tools, you can seamlessly integrate Paystack into your business and start accepting payments within minutes. You can also choose to use other Paystack features in our product suite, like recurring payments, invoicing, subscription billing, and split payments, so you can quickly and conveniently serve your customers' needs.

[https://www.youtube.com/embed/lio2A7UNccw](https://www.youtube.com/embed/lio2A7UNccw)

## Countries we serve

Our services are available only to businesses registered in [Nigeria](https://paystack.com/) 🇳🇬, [Ghana](https://paystack.com/gh/?localeUpdate=true) 🇬🇭, [South Africa](https://paystack.com/za/?localeUpdate=true)🇿🇦 and Kenya 🇰🇪, but we aim to serve merchants across Africa soon.

If we aren’t live in your country yet, you can subscribe to [our waitlist here](https://paystack.com/countries) to get a message from us as soon as we launch our services in your country. You can also [subscribe to the Paystack blog](https://paystack.com/blog) to avoid missing new product updates and announcements.

**Important to note**

We're currently running a private beta program in Côte d'Ivoire and Egypt. To learn more about the program and to join, [click here](https://paystack.com/blog/company-news/civ-rwanda-egypt-beta).

## What kinds of businesses can use Paystack?

Over 200,000 businesses across the continent — both registered and unregistered — use Paystack to process payments. Paystack has everything you need to meet your business goals at every scale level.

We cater to businesses from numerous industries, including banking & loan services, investment and savings services, hospitality services, transport companies, betting companies, religious organisations, NGOs, media companies, local e-commerce businesses and many more.

Companies like MTN and UPS in Nigeria, Betway and Safari Valley Resort in Ghana, Rentoza and Grandilla in South Africa, and ANDO Foods in Kenya trust Paystack to power their businesses.

## Real success stories: Paystack merchant case studies

Explore how our services have empowered businesses of all sizes to navigate challenges and capitalize on opportunities.

These real-world stories highlight our positive impact on businesses in Africa. With Paystack, you can go beyond simple payment collections to create an experience that will delight your customers and help you grow your business:

**How PiggyVest Powers Savings for Over 2 Million Nigerians With Paystack**

[https://www.youtube.com/embed/3mQ4tGPcEww](https://www.youtube.com/embed/3mQ4tGPcEww)

**How Moove uses Paystack to empower mobility entrepreneurs**

[https://www.youtube.com/embed/Q8OjxTDawIo](https://www.youtube.com/embed/Q8OjxTDawIo)

**How Granadilla Swim uses Paystack to take Cape Town swimwear global**

[https://www.youtube.com/embed/0dP3a9di-IM](https://www.youtube.com/embed/0dP3a9di-IM)

**How visual artist "Shutabug" sells art online with Paystack**

[https://www.youtube.com/embed/9RE05bp_jos](https://www.youtube.com/embed/9RE05bp_jos)

You can visit [this YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PL7p57jRcd2OzWEe_oRc9ayjFeNjnJfRP5&si=5bqIYNsL01WH4xmZ)for more merchant case studies and [our Wall of Love](https://paystack.com/wall-of-love) for a detailed list of our testimonials.

## Want to see Paystack in action?

Take our demo checkout for a spin at [paystack.com/demo](https://paystack.com/demo). Our live demo means real money will be withdrawn from your account. Please choose an amount you can afford to give away 😊

With our[interactive developer documentation](https://paystack.com/docs/), you can see how to receive payments, make transfers, and more with the Paystack API.

We also organize a webinar every two weeks to give merchants a live, guided tour of the powerful tools available on Paystack. To join the Paystack Live Demo Webinar, all you need to do is[register for it here](https://app.livestorm.co/paystack/live-demo).

### Related Articles

pages.title: Grow Your Business with Paystack Small Business… - The Paystack Blog
pages.text:
# Grow Your Business with Paystack Small Business…

Growing a business comes with new questions at every stage.

At first, the focus might be getting customers and accepting payments. Then come the next set of decisions: how to manage cash flow, improve operations, reach more customers, handle taxes, build better systems, and keep the business moving with more structure.

At Paystack, we work with thousands of businesses across different industries, and we know that small businesses need more than payment tools to grow well. They need practical support, useful knowledge, trusted guidance, and a community of other business owners building through similar challenges.

That’s why we’re introducing Small Business Launchpad.

Launchpad is a 4-week growth program for active Paystack merchants in Nigeria running small and medium-sized businesses. It’s designed to help selected businesses strengthen how they run, sell, manage money, serve customers, and grow.

Applications are now open for the first cohort, which begins on August 27, 2026.  

![Image](https://directus.paystack.co/assets/91dac10f-5416-4f43-b32c-2ede6d48b0ef)

## **What you’ll get**

Businesses selected for Small Business Launchpad will get access to practical support during and after the program, including:

### **3 months of free processing**

After completing the program, participants will receive 3 months of free processing on Paystack, capped at ₦25 million in processed payments.

### **Priority support**

Participants will receive priority support during the 4-week program, with faster help for payment questions, technical issues, product support, and other Paystack-related needs.

### **Business clinics**

Each cohort will join weekly business clinics led by experienced operators, Paystack team members, and subject-matter experts.

The clinics will cover practical topics such as finance, tax, marketing, operations, compliance, customer experience, and using Paystack products more effectively.

### **Expert office hours**

Participants will get access to office hours where they can ask specific questions about their business and receive guidance from people with relevant experience across finance, tax, customer experience, compliance, legal, marketing, and sales.

### **Welcome kit and completion certificate**

Each selected business will receive a Launchpad welcome kit to support them through the program. Businesses that complete the 4 weeks will also receive a Paystack Launchpad completion certificate.

### **Launchpad community and early product access**

After the program, participants will join the Launchpad community, where they can connect with other business owners, access useful updates and opportunities from Paystack, and be considered for early access to relevant Paystack product features.

## **Who can apply?**

Small Business Launchpad is open to active Paystack merchants in Nigeria running small and medium-sized businesses.

Each cohort will include up to 50 selected businesses. Applications will be reviewed to select businesses on a first come, first serve basis.

If your business isn’t on Paystack yet, [you can create a Paystack account](https://dashboard.paystack.com/#/signup?utm_source=blog&utm_campaign=small_business_bundle) and start building with us. Launchpad is one of the ways we’re giving businesses on Paystack access to more support as they grow.

## **Program fee**

Small Business Launchpad has a participation fee of ₦150,000 for selected businesses.

The fee helps us create a focused, high-commitment experience and deliver a strong program for every business in the cohort.

## **How to apply**

If you’re an active Paystack merchant in Nigeria running a small or medium-sized business, you can apply to join Paystack Launchpad.

To apply, [complete this application form](https://form.typeform.com/to/cAWAPkoR). If selected, you’ll receive the next steps by email.  

## **Build with more support**

Small Business Launchpad is one more way we’re supporting the businesses building with us.

Payments are important, but growth also depends on the decisions business owners make every day: how they manage money, serve customers, improve operations, market their products, and build systems that can last.

If your business is ready for its next stage, we’d love to hear from you.

## **Common questions**

**Do I need to be a Paystack merchant to apply?**

Yes. Small Business Launchpad is open to active Paystack merchants in Nigeria running small and medium-sized businesses.

If your business isn’t on Paystack yet, [you can create a Paystack account](https://dashboard.paystack.com/#/signup) and start building with us.

**How many businesses will be selected?**

Each Launchpad cohort will include up to 50 selected businesses.

**What does the participation fee cover?**

The fee gives selected businesses access to the full 4-week program, including business clinics, expert office hours, priority support, Paystack product benefits, a welcome kit, a completion certificate, and the Launchpad community.

Participants who complete the program will also receive 3 months of free Paystack processing, capped at ₦25 million in processed payments.

**What happens after I apply?**

We’ll review your application and contact selected businesses by email with the next steps.

**When do applications close?**Applications for the first Small Business Launchpad cohort close on August 6, 2026.

If you have more questions, kindly send us a message at [[email protected]](https://paystack.com/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#cf9c828dbfbda0a8bdaea2bc8fbfaeb6bcbbaeaca4e1aca0a2). We’re happy to help 💙
